title: Secure Multi-Tier Virtual Network with Subnets and NSGs
summary: Architect a segmented virtual network with web and database subnets, then enforce traffic isolation using Network Security Groups (NSGs) and Application Security Groups (ASGs).
scenarioTemplate: You are designing network infrastructure for an application in '{{region}}'. You must deploy a Virtual Network named '{{vnetName}}' with address space '{{vnetPrefix}}'. Inside, create two subnets: a web tier subnet ('{{webSubnetName}}', {{webSubnetPrefix}}) and a database tier subnet ('{{dbSubnetName}}', {{dbSubnetPrefix}}). Configure an NSG named '{{nsgName}}' to allow inbound port {{webPort}} to the web tier, while completely blocking the database tier from direct public Internet exposure.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{region}}'.
Create Virtual Network '{{vnetName}}' with CIDR '{{vnetPrefix}}'.
Add frontend subnet '{{webSubnetName}}' ({{webSubnetPrefix}}) and backend subnet '{{dbSubnetName}}' ({{dbSubnetPrefix}}).
Create Network Security Group '{{nsgName}}' with an Inbound rule allowing TCP port {{webPort}} with priority 200.
Associate '{{nsgName}}' to subnet '{{webSubnetName}}'.
Verify effective NSG associations on the subnet.

steps.title: Create Resource Group and Segmented Virtual Network
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Virtual networks** > **+ Create**. Resource group: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{vnetName}}`, Region: `{{region}}`. Under **IP addresses**, set address space to `{{vnetPrefix}}`. Add subnet `{{webSubnetName}}` with range `{{webSubnetPrefix}}`, then add subnet `{{dbSubnetName}}` with range `{{dbSubnetPrefix}}`.
steps.cliCommand:
az group create --name {{resourceGroup}} --location {{region}}

az network vnet create \
  --name {{vnetName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --address-prefixes {{vnetPrefix}} \
  --subnet-name {{webSubnetName}} \
  --subnet-prefixes {{webSubnetPrefix}}

az network vnet subnet create \
  --name {{dbSubnetName}} \
  --vnet-name {{vnetName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --address-prefixes {{dbSubnetPrefix}}
steps.validation: az network vnet subnet list --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --vnet-name {{vnetName}} -o table

steps.title: Create Network Security Group and Inbound Port Rule
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Network security groups** > **+ Create**. Select RG `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{nsgName}}`, Region: `{{region}}`. Once deployed, open the NSG > **Inbound security rules** > **+ Add**. Source: Any, Destination: Any, Destination port: `{{webPort}}`, Protocol: TCP, Action: Allow, Priority: 200, Name: `Allow_Web_{{webPort}}`.
steps.cliCommand:
az network nsg create \
  --name {{nsgName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}}

az network nsg rule create \
  --name Allow_Web_{{webPort}} \
  --nsg-name {{nsgName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --priority 200 \
  --access Allow \
  --direction Inbound \
  --protocol Tcp \
  --destination-port-ranges {{webPort}}
steps.validation: az network nsg rule show --nsg-name {{nsgName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --name Allow_Web_{{webPort}} --query '{Access:access, Port:destinationPortRange, Priority:priority}' -o table

steps.title: Associate Network Security Group to Web Subnet
steps.portalGuide: In the NSG blade, select **Subnets** > **+ Associate**. Choose Virtual network: `{{vnetName}}`, Subnet: `{{webSubnetName}}` > click **OK**.
steps.cliCommand:
az network vnet subnet update \
  --name {{webSubnetName}} \
  --vnet-name {{vnetName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --network-security-group {{nsgName}}
steps.validation: az network vnet subnet show --name {{webSubnetName}} --vnet-name {{vnetName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query 'networkSecurityGroup.id' -o tsv

steps.title: Clean Up Lab Resources
steps.portalGuide: Navigate to **Resource groups** > `{{resourceGroup}}` > click **Delete resource group**.
steps.cliCommand: az group delete --name {{resourceGroup}} --yes --no-wait
steps.validation: az group exists --name {{resourceGroup}}

title: Configure Global and Regional Virtual Network Peering
summary: Connect two Virtual Networks with non-overlapping IP address spaces via bidirectional VNet Peering to enable low-latency private connectivity.
scenarioTemplate: You are interconnecting workloads across environments. The Hub network is located in '{{hubRegion}}' with address space '{{hubPrefix}}', while the Spoke network resides in '{{spokeRegion}}' with address space '{{spokePrefix}}'. You must deploy both networks inside '{{resourceGroup}}' and establish full bidirectional VNet peering ('{{hubToSpokePeering}}' and '{{spokeToHubPeering}}') enabling virtual network access and forwarded traffic.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{hubRegion}}'.
Deploy Hub VNet '{{hubVnetName}}' in '{{hubRegion}}' with prefix '{{hubPrefix}}'.
Deploy Spoke VNet '{{spokeVnetName}}' in '{{spokeRegion}}' with prefix '{{spokePrefix}}'.
Configure peering from '{{hubVnetName}}' to '{{spokeVnetName}}'.
Configure return peering from '{{spokeVnetName}}' to '{{hubVnetName}}'.
Verify both peering links transition to the 'Connected' status.

steps.title: Create Hub and Spoke Virtual Networks
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Virtual networks** > **+ Create**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{hubVnetName}}`, Region: `{{hubRegion}}`, IP Space: `{{hubPrefix}}`. Repeat for Spoke: Name: `{{spokeVnetName}}`, Region: `{{spokeRegion}}`, IP Space: `{{spokePrefix}}`.
steps.cliCommand:
az group create --name {{resourceGroup}} --location {{hubRegion}}

az network vnet create \
  --name {{hubVnetName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{hubRegion}} \
  --address-prefixes {{hubPrefix}} \
  --subnet-name snet-default \
  --subnet-prefixes 10.100.1.0/24

az network vnet create \
  --name {{spokeVnetName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{spokeRegion}} \
  --address-prefixes {{spokePrefix}} \
  --subnet-name snet-default \
  --subnet-prefixes 10.200.1.0/24
steps.validation: az network vnet list --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query "[].{Name:name, Location:location, CIDR:addressSpace.addressPrefixes[0]}" -o table

steps.title: Configure Bidirectional VNet Peering Links
steps.portalGuide: Open `{{hubVnetName}}` > **Peerings** (under Settings) > **+ Add**. Peering link name: `{{hubToSpokePeering}}`. Remote virtual network: choose `{{spokeVnetName}}`. Name of remote peering link: `{{spokeToHubPeering}}`. Ensure 'Allow virtual network access' is checked on both > click **Add**.
steps.cliCommand:
HUB_ID=$(az network vnet show --name {{hubVnetName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query id -o tsv)
SPOKE_ID=$(az network vnet show --name {{spokeVnetName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query id -o tsv)

az network vnet peering create \
  --name {{hubToSpokePeering}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --vnet-name {{hubVnetName}} \
  --remote-vnet "$SPOKE_ID" \
  --allow-vnet-access

az network vnet peering create \
  --name {{spokeToHubPeering}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --vnet-name {{spokeVnetName}} \
  --remote-vnet "$HUB_ID" \
  --allow-vnet-access
steps.validation: az network vnet peering list --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --vnet-name {{hubVnetName}} --query "[].{Name:name, Status:peeringState}" -o table

steps.title: Verify Effective Peering State
steps.portalGuide: Review the **Peerings** tab on both VNets. Ensure Peering status states **Connected** on both sides (not Initiated).
steps.cliCommand:
az network vnet peering show --name {{hubToSpokePeering}} --vnet-name {{hubVnetName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query '{HubSide:peeringState}' -o table
az network vnet peering show --name {{spokeToHubPeering}} --vnet-name {{spokeVnetName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query '{SpokeSide:peeringState}' -o table
steps.validation: echo "Verified bidirectional Connected state."

steps.title: Clean Up Lab Resources
steps.portalGuide: Delete resource group `{{resourceGroup}}`.
steps.cliCommand: az group delete --name {{resourceGroup}} --yes --no-wait
steps.validation: az group exists --name {{resourceGroup}}

title: Implement Azure Private DNS Zones with Virtual Network Links
summary: Configure authoritative internal name resolution using Azure Private DNS Zones, Virtual Network links, and automatic VM registration.
scenarioTemplate: Your cloud migration team requires private internal DNS resolution without deploying custom IaaS DNS servers. In resource group '{{resourceGroup}}', provision a Virtual Network '{{vnetName}}' in '{{region}}'. Create a Private DNS Zone named '{{privateZoneName}}', establish a Virtual Network Link named '{{vnetLinkName}}' with auto-registration enabled, and add static DNS records for a database host ('{{recordHost}}' -> {{recordIp}}).
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{region}}'.
Deploy Virtual Network '{{vnetName}}' (10.20.0.0/16).
Deploy Private DNS Zone '{{privateZoneName}}'.
Create a Virtual Network Link '{{vnetLinkName}}' attaching '{{vnetName}}' to '{{privateZoneName}}' with registrationEnabled set to true.
Add an A Record for '{{recordHost}}' pointing to '{{recordIp}}'.
Verify the DNS record set exists and inspect zone configuration.

steps.title: Create Resource Group and Virtual Network
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Virtual networks** > **+ Create**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{vnetName}}`, Region: `{{region}}`, CIDR: `10.20.0.0/16` > **Review + create** > **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
az group create --name {{resourceGroup}} --location {{region}}
az network vnet create \
  --name {{vnetName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --address-prefixes 10.20.0.0/16 \
  --subnet-name snet-workload \
  --subnet-prefixes 10.20.1.0/24
steps.validation: az network vnet show --name {{vnetName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query 'provisioningState' -o tsv

steps.title: Deploy Azure Private DNS Zone
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Private DNS zones** > **+ Create**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{privateZoneName}}` > click **Review + create** > **Create**.
steps.validation: az network private-dns zone show --name {{privateZoneName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query '{Zone:name, Records:numberOfRecordSets}' -o table

steps.title: Link Virtual Network and Create DNS A Record
steps.portalGuide: In the Private DNS Zone `{{privateZoneName}}`, select **Virtual network links** > **+ Add**. Link name: `{{vnetLinkName}}`, Virtual network: `{{vnetName}}`, Check **Enable auto registration** > click **OK**. Then go to **Record sets** > **+ Add**. Name: `{{recordHost}}`, Type: **A**, IP address: `{{recordIp}}` > click **OK**.
steps.cliCommand:
VNET_ID=$(az network vnet show --name {{vnetName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query id -o tsv)

# Create VNet Link with Auto-Registration:
az network private-dns link vnet create \
  --name {{vnetLinkName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --zone-name {{privateZoneName}} \
  --virtual-network "$VNET_ID" \
  --registration-enabled true

# Create DNS A Record:
az network private-dns record-set a add-record \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --zone-name {{privateZoneName}} \
  --record-set-name {{recordHost}} \
  --ipv4-address {{recordIp}}
steps.validation: az network private-dns record-set a show --name {{recordHost}} --zone-name {{privateZoneName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query '{Name:name, IP:aRecords[0].ipv4Address}' -o table

steps.title: Clean Up Lab Resources
steps.portalGuide: Delete resource group `{{resourceGroup}}`.
steps.cliCommand: az group delete --name {{resourceGroup}} --yes --no-wait
steps.validation: az group exists --name {{resourceGroup}}

title: Deploy Azure Bastion for Secure Browser-Based VM Administration
summary: Provision the dedicated AzureBastionSubnet and deploy Azure Bastion Host to allow secure RDP and SSH connectivity over TLS without exposing public IPs.
scenarioTemplate: In compliance with zero-exposure security policies in '{{region}}', administrators must not assign public IP addresses directly to virtual machine network interfaces. You must prepare Virtual Network '{{vnetName}}' in '{{resourceGroup}}' by creating the required 'AzureBastionSubnet' subnet with CIDR '{{bastionPrefix}}', provision a Standard Public IP named '{{publicIpName}}', and deploy an Azure Bastion Host named '{{bastionName}}'.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{region}}'.
Deploy Virtual Network '{{vnetName}}' with a workload subnet.
Add a subnet named strictly 'AzureBastionSubnet' with prefix '{{bastionPrefix}}' (/26 minimum).
Deploy a Public IP '{{publicIpName}}' with SKU Standard and Allocation method Static.
Provision Azure Bastion Host '{{bastionName}}' attached to 'AzureBastionSubnet' and '{{publicIpName}}'.
Verify the Bastion Host provisioningState is Succeeded.

steps.title: Create Virtual Network and Dedicated AzureBastionSubnet
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Virtual networks** > **+ Create**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{vnetName}}`, Region: `{{region}}`. Add default subnet `snet-workload` (10.0.0.0/24). Add a second subnet named **AzureBastionSubnet** with prefix `{{bastionPrefix}}` > Click **Review + create** > **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
az group create --name {{resourceGroup}} --location {{region}}

az network vnet create \
  --name {{vnetName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --address-prefixes 10.0.0.0/16 \
  --subnet-name snet-workload \
  --subnet-prefixes 10.0.0.0/24

az network vnet subnet create \
  --name AzureBastionSubnet \
  --vnet-name {{vnetName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --address-prefixes {{bastionPrefix}}
steps.validation: az network vnet subnet show --name AzureBastionSubnet --vnet-name {{vnetName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query 'addressPrefix' -o tsv

steps.title: Create Standard Public IP for Bastion
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Public IP addresses** > **+ Create**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{publicIpName}}`, Region: `{{region}}`, SKU: **Standard**, Tier: Regional, Assignment: **Static** > click **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
az network public-ip create \
  --name {{publicIpName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --sku Standard \
  --allocation-method Static
steps.validation: az network public-ip show --name {{publicIpName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query '{IP:ipAddress, Sku:sku.name}' -o table

steps.title: Deploy Azure Bastion Host
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Bastions** > **+ Create**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{bastionName}}`, Region: `{{region}}`, Tier: **Basic** (or Standard). Virtual network: `{{vnetName}}` (it will auto-detect AzureBastionSubnet). Public IP address: select existing `{{publicIpName}}` > click **Review + create** > **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
az network bastion create \
  --name {{bastionName}} \
  --public-ip-address {{publicIpName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --vnet-name {{vnetName}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --sku Basic
steps.validation: az network bastion show --name {{bastionName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query '{Name:name, Provisioning:provisioningState, Sku:sku.name}' -o table

steps.title: Clean Up Lab Resources
steps.portalGuide: Delete resource group `{{resourceGroup}}`.
steps.cliCommand: az group delete --name {{resourceGroup}} --yes --no-wait
steps.validation: az group exists --name {{resourceGroup}}

title: Configure Azure Public Standard Load Balancer and Health Probes
summary: Implement layer-4 load balancing using Azure Standard Load Balancer, frontend IP configuration, backend address pools, and health probes.
scenarioTemplate: You are deploying a scalable web service in '{{region}}'. To distribute incoming web traffic across virtual machines, create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}', provision a Public Standard Load Balancer named '{{lbName}}' with public IP '{{publicIpName}}', configure a backend address pool named '{{backendPoolName}}', set up an HTTP health probe monitoring port {{probePort}}, and configure a load-balancing rule for port {{lbPort}}.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{region}}'.
Deploy a Standard Public IP named '{{publicIpName}}'.
Deploy Standard Load Balancer '{{lbName}}' with frontend IP bound to '{{publicIpName}}'.
Create backend address pool '{{backendPoolName}}'.
Create an HTTP Health Probe named 'hp-web' monitoring port {{probePort}} every 5 seconds.
Configure a load balancing rule 'lbrule-http' forwarding port {{lbPort}} to backend pool {{backendPoolName}} with probe 'hp-web'.

steps.title: Create Resource Group and Public IP
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Resource groups** > **+ Create**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Region: `{{region}}`. Search for **Public IP addresses** > **+ Create**. Name: `{{publicIpName}}`, SKU: Standard, Assignment: Static.
steps.cliCommand:
az group create --name {{resourceGroup}} --location {{region}}

az network public-ip create \
  --name {{publicIpName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --sku Standard \
  --allocation-method Static
steps.validation: az network public-ip show --name {{publicIpName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query 'ipAddress' -o tsv

steps.title: Create Standard Load Balancer and Backend Pool
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Load balancers** > **+ Create**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{lbName}}`, Region: `{{region}}`, SKU: Standard, Type: **Public**. Frontend IP configuration: Add `{{publicIpName}}`. In **Backend pools**, add pool named `{{backendPoolName}}` > click **Review + create** > **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
az network lb create \
  --name {{lbName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --sku Standard \
  --public-ip-address {{publicIpName}} \
  --frontend-ip-name LoadBalancerFrontend \
  --backend-pool-name {{backendPoolName}}
steps.validation: az network lb show --name {{lbName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query '{Name:name, Sku:sku.name}' -o table

steps.title: Create Health Probe and Load Balancing Rule
steps.portalGuide: Open `{{lbName}}` > **Health probes** > **+ Add**. Name: `hp-web`, Protocol: **HTTP**, Port: `{{probePort}}`, Path: `/`, Interval: `5`. Then open **Load balancing rules** > **+ Add**. Name: `lbrule-http`, Frontend IP: `LoadBalancerFrontend`, Protocol: TCP, Port: `{{lbPort}}`, Backend port: `{{lbPort}}`, Backend pool: `{{backendPoolName}}`, Health probe: `hp-web` > click **Save**.
steps.cliCommand:
# Create Health Probe:
az network lb probe create \
  --lb-name {{lbName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --name hp-web \
  --protocol Http \
  --port {{probePort}} \
  --path / \
  --interval 5

# Create Load Balancing Rule:
az network lb rule create \
  --lb-name {{lbName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --name lbrule-http \
  --frontend-ip-name LoadBalancerFrontend \
  --backend-pool-name {{backendPoolName}} \
  --probe-name hp-web \
  --protocol Tcp \
  --frontend-port {{lbPort}} \
  --backend-port {{lbPort}}
steps.powershellCommand:
$lb = Get-AzLoadBalancer -ResourceGroupName '{{resourceGroup}}' -Name '{{lbName}}'
$probe = Add-AzLoadBalancerProbeConfig -LoadBalancer $lb -Name 'hp-web' -Protocol Http -Port {{probePort}} -RequestPath '/' -IntervalInSeconds 5 -ProbeCount 2
$rule = Add-AzLoadBalancerRuleConfig -LoadBalancer $lb -Name 'lbrule-http' -FrontendIpConfiguration ($lb.FrontendIpConfigurations[0]) -BackendAddressPool ($lb.BackendAddressPools[0]) -Probe ($lb.Probes[0]) -Protocol Tcp -FrontendPort {{lbPort}} -BackendPort {{lbPort}}
$lb | Set-AzLoadBalancer
steps.validation: az network lb rule show --lb-name {{lbName}} --name lbrule-http --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query '{Rule:name, FrontendPort:frontendPort, BackendPort:backendPort}' -o table

steps.title: Clean Up Lab Resources
steps.portalGuide: Delete resource group `{{resourceGroup}}`.
steps.cliCommand: az group delete --name {{resourceGroup}} --yes --no-wait
steps.validation: az group exists --name {{resourceGroup}}

title: Deploy Azure Application Gateway with Path-Based Routing
summary: Configure Layer 7 routing and SSL/TLS delivery controller using Azure Application Gateway with URL path map rules and health probes.
scenarioTemplate: You are hosting a microservice architecture in '{{region}}'. To direct user requests based on URL path, you must create a Virtual Network '{{vnetName}}' with dedicated subnet 'AppGatewaySubnet' ({{appGwSubnetPrefix}}), provision an Application Gateway Standard_v2 named '{{gatewayName}}', configure backend pools for image services and API services, and create path-based routing rules directing '/images/*' to pool 1 and '/api/*' to pool 2.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{region}}'.
Deploy Virtual Network '{{vnetName}}' containing subnet 'AppGatewaySubnet' ({{appGwSubnetPrefix}}).
Create a Standard SKU Public IP named '{{publicIpName}}'.
Deploy Application Gateway Standard_v2 named '{{gatewayName}}'.
Configure multiple backend pools and verify URL Path Map configuration.
Inspect Application Gateway routing rules and clean up resources.

steps.title: Create Virtual Network and AppGatewaySubnet
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Virtual networks** > **+ Create**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{vnetName}}`, Region: `{{region}}`. Add subnet `AppGatewaySubnet` with prefix `{{appGwSubnetPrefix}}`. Add backend subnet `snet-backend` with prefix `10.0.2.0/24`.
steps.cliCommand:
az group create --name {{resourceGroup}} --location {{region}}

az network vnet create \
  --name {{vnetName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --address-prefixes 10.0.0.0/16 \
  --subnet-name AppGatewaySubnet \
  --subnet-prefixes {{appGwSubnetPrefix}}

az network vnet subnet create \
  --name snet-backend \
  --vnet-name {{vnetName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --address-prefixes 10.0.2.0/24
steps.validation: az network vnet subnet show --name AppGatewaySubnet --vnet-name {{vnetName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query 'addressPrefix' -o tsv

steps.title: Deploy Standard Public IP and Application Gateway
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Application gateways** > **+ Create**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{gatewayName}}`, Region: `{{region}}`, Tier: **Standard V2**. Virtual network: `{{vnetName}}`, Subnet: `AppGatewaySubnet`. Frontend: Public IP (create new `{{publicIpName}}`). Backend: Add `bepool-images` and `bepool-api` > Click **Review + create** > **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
az network public-ip create \
  --name {{publicIpName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --sku Standard \
  --allocation-method Static

az network application-gateway create \
  --name {{gatewayName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --sku Standard_v2 \
  --capacity 1 \
  --vnet-name {{vnetName}} \
  --subnet AppGatewaySubnet \
  --public-ip-address {{publicIpName}} \
  --frontend-port 80 \
  --http-settings-port 80 \
  --http-settings-protocol Http
steps.powershellCommand:
# Deploy Application Gateway via Azure CLI or PowerShell cmdlet
az network application-gateway show --name {{gatewayName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}}
steps.validation: az network application-gateway show --name {{gatewayName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query '{Name:name, Tier:sku.name, State:provisioningState}' -o table

steps.title: Configure URL Path-Based Routing Rule
steps.portalGuide: In `{{gatewayName}}`, select **Backend pools** > **+ Add** `bepool-images`. Add `bepool-api`. Select **Routing rules** > select rule > Path-based routing > Add path `/images/*` target `bepool-images` and `/api/*` target `bepool-api` > click **Save**.
steps.cliCommand:
# Add backend pools:
az network application-gateway address-pool create \
  --gateway-name {{gatewayName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --name bepool-images

az network application-gateway address-pool create \
  --gateway-name {{gatewayName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --name bepool-api
steps.validation: az network application-gateway address-pool list --gateway-name {{gatewayName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query "[].name" -o table

steps.title: Clean Up Lab Resources
steps.portalGuide: Delete resource group `{{resourceGroup}}`.
steps.cliCommand: az group delete --name {{resourceGroup}} --yes --no-wait
steps.validation: az group exists --name {{resourceGroup}}

title: Implement User-Defined Routes (UDRs) and Virtual Routing Tables
summary: Override default system routing by authoring custom Azure Route Tables with User-Defined Routes (UDRs) directing traffic to a firewall or NVA.
scenarioTemplate: Security policy requires forcing all outbound internet traffic from a workload subnet in '{{region}}' through an inspection firewall / Network Virtual Appliance (NVA) at private IP '{{nvaIp}}'. You must create a Route Table named '{{routeTableName}}' in '{{resourceGroup}}', configure a User-Defined Route named '{{routeName}}' routing '{{targetRoutePrefix}}' to next hop type VirtualAppliance, and associate the route table with subnet '{{subnetName}}'.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{region}}'.
Deploy Virtual Network '{{vnetName}}' with subnet '{{subnetName}}' (10.0.2.0/24).
Create Route Table '{{routeTableName}}'.
Add User-Defined Route '{{routeName}}' for address prefix '{{targetRoutePrefix}}' with nextHopType 'VirtualAppliance' and nextHopIpAddress '{{nvaIp}}'.
Associate '{{routeTableName}}' with subnet '{{subnetName}}'.
Verify effective route table association on the subnet.

steps.title: Create Virtual Network and Subnet
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Virtual networks** > **+ Create**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{vnetName}}`, Region: `{{region}}`. Add subnet `{{subnetName}}` with prefix `10.0.2.0/24`.
steps.cliCommand:
az group create --name {{resourceGroup}} --location {{region}}

az network vnet create \
  --name {{vnetName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --address-prefixes 10.0.0.0/16 \
  --subnet-name {{subnetName}} \
  --subnet-prefixes 10.0.2.0/24
steps.validation: az network vnet subnet show --name {{subnetName}} --vnet-name {{vnetName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query 'provisioningState' -o tsv

steps.title: Create Route Table and Add User-Defined Route
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Route tables** > **+ Create**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{routeTableName}}`, Region: `{{region}}`. Once deployed, open the Route Table > **Routes** > **+ Add**. Route name: `{{routeName}}`, Destination type: **IP Addresses**, Destination IP addresses/CIDR ranges: `{{targetRoutePrefix}}`, Next hop type: **Virtual appliance**, Next hop address: `{{nvaIp}}` > click **Add**.
steps.cliCommand:
az network route-table create \
  --name {{routeTableName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}}

az network route-table route create \
  --name {{routeName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --route-table-name {{routeTableName}} \
  --address-prefix {{targetRoutePrefix}} \
  --next-hop-type VirtualAppliance \
  --next-hop-ip-address {{nvaIp}}
steps.validation: az network route-table route list --route-table-name {{routeTableName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query "[].{Name:name, Prefix:addressPrefix, NextHop:nextHopType, NextHopIP:nextHopIpAddress}" -o table

steps.title: Associate Route Table to Subnet
steps.portalGuide: In `{{routeTableName}}`, select **Subnets** > **+ Associate**. Virtual network: `{{vnetName}}`, Subnet: `{{subnetName}}` > click **OK**.
steps.cliCommand:
az network vnet subnet update \
  --name {{subnetName}} \
  --vnet-name {{vnetName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --route-table {{routeTableName}}
steps.validation: az network vnet subnet show --name {{subnetName}} --vnet-name {{vnetName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query 'routeTable.id' -o tsv

steps.title: Clean Up Lab Resources
steps.portalGuide: Delete resource group `{{resourceGroup}}`.
steps.cliCommand: az group delete --name {{resourceGroup}} --yes --no-wait
steps.validation: az group exists --name {{resourceGroup}}
